title: Harbor billing service
summary: Go service that issues invoices and handles payment webhooks
body: Harbor lives in the billing/harbor repo. Go 1.23, Postgres 16, owned by the payments team. Exposes a gRPC API to the storefront and consumes webhooks from the card processor.

title: Lumen analytics dashboard
summary: React and TypeScript dashboard for product metrics
body: Lumen is the internal metrics UI. Vite build, React 18, charts drawn with visx. Reads from the Orrery feature API and renders weekly retention cohorts.

title: Tidepool data pipeline
summary: Airflow DAGs that load warehouse tables nightly
body: Tidepool runs on Airflow 2.9. Nightly DAGs pull from the OLTP replicas into the warehouse, then run dbt models. A failed DAG pages the data on-call.

title: Quill documentation site
summary: Static docs site built with Astro and deployed to the CDN
body: Quill renders the public developer docs from markdown in the quill-docs repo. Astro 4, search by Pagefind, preview builds for every pull request.

title: Brindle mobile app
summary: Kotlin Multiplatform app for iOS and Android
body: Brindle shares business logic in Kotlin Multiplatform with native Compose and SwiftUI shells. Releases ship every second Tuesday through TestFlight and the Play internal track.

title: Cairn infrastructure repo
summary: Terraform modules for networks, clusters and DNS
body: Cairn holds all Terraform. State is remote with locking, one workspace per environment. Changes need a plan reviewed by a second engineer before apply.

title: Orrery feature store
summary: Python service serving ML features with low latency
body: Orrery serves precomputed model features over HTTP. FastAPI plus Redis for hot keys, parquet snapshots in object storage for backfills. p99 target is 20 ms.

title: Sundial scheduler
summary: Rust cron replacement that triggers internal jobs
body: Sundial reads job definitions from YAML, fires them through the queue and records run history in SQLite. Written in Rust, single static binary.

title: Mosaic design system
summary: Shared component library and tokens for all web apps
body: Mosaic publishes @acme/mosaic to the private registry. Tokens come from Figma exports; components are tested with Storybook and Chromatic snapshots.

title: Lantern auth gateway
summary: OIDC gateway in front of internal tools
body: Lantern terminates single sign-on for internal web tools using OIDC against the corporate identity provider. Sessions last 8 hours; group claims map to tool roles.

title: Ferrule CLI
summary: Developer command line for scaffolding services
body: Ferrule generates service skeletons, wires CI and registers the service in the catalog. Distributed as a Homebrew tap; written in Go with cobra.

title: Pavilion storefront
summary: Next.js customer storefront
body: Pavilion is the public shop. Next.js 14 app router, product data from the catalog API, checkout calls Harbor. Deployed on the edge runtime.

title: Catalog API
summary: GraphQL service for products, prices and inventory
body: Catalog API is a GraphQL layer over the product database and the inventory service. Persisted queries only in production; schema changes go through a contract check.

title: Notifier service
summary: Sends email, push and SMS from queue messages
body: Notifier consumes the notifications queue and fans out to the email vendor, push gateway and SMS provider. Templates live in the notifier-templates repo; rate limits are per channel.

title: Ledgerlint checker
summary: Nightly job that reconciles invoices against payouts
body: Ledgerlint compares Harbor invoices with bank payout files and opens a ticket for every mismatch over one cent. Runs at 03:00 UTC on the batch cluster.

title: Beacon feature flags
summary: Self-hosted flag service with a Go SDK and JS SDK
body: Beacon stores flags in Postgres and streams changes over SSE. SDKs cache locally so a Beacon outage never blocks a request. Flags older than 90 days are reported for cleanup.

title: Sieve search service
summary: OpenSearch wrapper for product and docs search
body: Sieve wraps an OpenSearch cluster and exposes a small query API. Synonyms are managed in synonyms.txt and reloaded without downtime. Reindexing takes about 40 minutes.

title: Warden secrets broker
summary: Wraps Vault to hand out short-lived credentials
body: Warden issues database and cloud credentials with a 1 hour lease. Services authenticate with their Kubernetes service account. Never paste secrets in tickets; request a lease instead.

title: Trellis CI templates
summary: Reusable GitHub Actions workflows
body: Trellis provides reusable workflows for build, test, scan and deploy. Pin to a major tag, for example trellis/build@v3. Caching uses the shared runner cache bucket.

title: Gazetteer service catalog
summary: Backstage instance listing every service and owner
body: Gazetteer is our Backstage portal. Every repo needs a catalog-info.yaml with owner, lifecycle and on-call link. Ferrule fills it in at scaffold time.

title: Quartz reporting jobs
summary: Monthly finance exports in Python
body: Quartz builds the month-end finance exports as CSV and uploads them to the finance bucket on the third business day. Uses pandas and a pinned Python 3.11.

title: Rookery chat bot
summary: Slack bot that answers on-call and deploy questions
body: Rookery is a Slack bot with slash commands for deploy status, who-is-on-call and incident creation. TypeScript on Bolt, runs as a single replica.

title: Meridian geo service
summary: Address validation and geocoding wrapper
body: Meridian caches geocoder responses for 30 days and falls back to a second vendor on timeout. Used by Pavilion checkout and the driver app.

title: Tern driver app
summary: Android app for delivery drivers
body: Tern is the driver-facing Android app. Offline-first with Room, syncs routes when connectivity returns, uses Meridian for address lookups.

title: Kiln image builder
summary: Builds hardened base container images weekly
body: Kiln rebuilds the distroless base images every Sunday, scans them and publishes digests. Services should reference the digest, not the tag.

title: Plover load tests
summary: k6 scripts for pre-release load testing
body: Plover holds the k6 scenarios for checkout, search and login. Run against staging before a major release; target is 500 requests per second with p95 under 300 ms.

title: Atlas data catalog
summary: Metadata catalog for warehouse tables
body: Atlas documents warehouse tables, column owners and PII tags. Tidepool publishes lineage into Atlas after every dbt run.

title: Heron status page
summary: Public status page fed by synthetic checks
body: Heron shows public component status. Synthetic checks run every minute from three regions; incident updates are posted by the incident commander.

title: Compass roadmap tool
summary: Internal planning board with quarterly goals
body: Compass tracks quarterly objectives and links them to epics. Goals are reviewed in the first week of each quarter.

title: Saffron email templates
summary: MJML templates for transactional email
body: Saffron stores MJML sources and compiles them to HTML on release. Always send a rendering test to the litmus inbox before changing the order confirmation.

title: Bellows autoscaler
summary: Custom queue-depth autoscaler for workers
body: Bellows scales worker deployments from queue depth rather than CPU. Cooldown is 5 minutes, max replicas capped per queue in bellows.yaml.

title: Juniper onboarding site
summary: New-hire checklist and laptop setup guide
body: Juniper is the onboarding portal: access requests, laptop checklist and team intro schedule. Content is markdown in the people-ops repo.

title: Marlin fraud rules
summary: Rule engine scoring risky orders
body: Marlin scores orders with a rules engine plus a small gradient-boosted model. Orders above 0.85 are held for manual review; rules are hot-reloaded.

title: Developer laptop setup
summary: Apple silicon laptops with Homebrew, asdf and direnv
body: Standard laptop is a 14-inch Apple silicon machine. Tool versions managed by asdf, per-repo env vars by direnv, packages by Homebrew. Disk encryption must be on.

title: VPN access
summary: WireGuard profile required for staging and databases
body: Staging and database hosts are reachable only over the WireGuard VPN. Request a profile through the access portal; profiles expire after 90 days.

title: Kubernetes clusters
summary: Three clusters: dev, stage and prod in two regions
body: Clusters are named kube-dev, kube-stage and kube-prod, running Kubernetes 1.30. Prod spans eu-west-1 and us-east-1. kubectl contexts are set by the cairn bootstrap script.

title: Container registry
summary: Private registry at registry.example.internal
body: Images are pushed to registry.example.internal under the team namespace. Retention keeps the last 30 tags per repository; digests referenced by deployments are never pruned.

title: Postgres fleet
summary: Managed Postgres 16 with read replicas
body: Primary databases are managed Postgres 16 with one synchronous replica and two read replicas. Connection pooling through PgBouncer in transaction mode; max 200 connections per service.

title: Redis clusters
summary: Redis 7 clusters for caching and rate limits
body: Two Redis 7 clusters: cache-redis (eviction allkeys-lru) and state-redis (no eviction, persistence on). Never store durable data in cache-redis.

title: Message queue
summary: NATS JetStream for service events
body: Service events flow through NATS JetStream. Streams are retained for 7 days; consumers must be idempotent because delivery is at least once.

title: Observability stack
summary: Prometheus, Grafana and Loki, traces in Tempo
body: Metrics in Prometheus with 30 day retention, dashboards in Grafana, logs in Loki, traces in Tempo. OpenTelemetry collectors run as a daemonset.

title: On-call tooling
summary: PagerDuty rotations with Slack escalation
body: Pages go through PagerDuty. Primary has 5 minutes to acknowledge before the secondary is paged. The weekly handoff happens Monday 10:00 in the on-call channel.

title: DNS and domains
summary: Internal zone example.internal managed in Cairn
body: Internal names live in the example.internal zone, public names in example.com. Records are code in Cairn; do not edit them in the console. TTL defaults to 300 seconds.

title: CDN configuration
summary: Edge cache with 10 minute default TTL
body: The CDN caches static assets for 10 minutes by default and honours surrogate-control headers. Purge by tag from the Quill and Pavilion deploy jobs.

title: CI runners
summary: Self-hosted ARM runners plus hosted x86
body: Builds run on self-hosted ARM runners in kube-dev by default. x86 jobs use hosted runners. Concurrency is capped at 40 jobs; queue time over 5 minutes should be reported.

title: Secrets handling
summary: Secrets come from Warden, never from env files in git
body: Secrets are injected at runtime from Warden. Committing .env files is blocked by a pre-commit hook and a CI scan. Rotate any leaked credential immediately and file a security ticket.

title: Python toolchain
summary: Python 3.12 with uv and ruff
body: New Python services use Python 3.12, uv for dependency management and ruff for linting and formatting. Quartz is the exception and stays on 3.11.

title: Node toolchain
summary: Node 22 LTS with pnpm workspaces
body: Front-end repos use Node 22 LTS and pnpm. Lockfiles are committed; CI runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile.

title: Go toolchain
summary: Go 1.23 with golangci-lint
body: Go services build with Go 1.23 and are linted by golangci-lint using the shared config from Trellis. Modules are vendored for release builds.

title: Editor conventions
summary: EditorConfig and format on save
body: Every repo ships an .editorconfig: LF line endings, 2-space indent for web and 4 for Python. Editors should format on save with the repo formatter.

title: Database backups
summary: Nightly snapshots with 35 day retention
body: Postgres snapshots run nightly at 01:00 UTC and are kept 35 days, with weekly copies in a second region for one year. Restore drills happen quarterly.

title: Object storage buckets
summary: Buckets per environment with lifecycle rules
body: Object storage buckets are named acme-<env>-<purpose>. Lifecycle rules move data to infrequent access after 30 days. Public buckets are forbidden except the Quill assets bucket.

title: TLS certificates
summary: cert-manager issues certificates automatically
body: cert-manager requests and renews certificates from the internal ACME endpoint 30 days before expiry. Alerts fire at 14 days remaining if renewal fails.

title: SSH access policy
summary: Short-lived SSH certificates, no static keys
body: Hosts accept only short-lived SSH certificates signed by the internal CA, valid 8 hours. Static authorized_keys entries are removed by configuration management.

title: Time conventions
summary: All systems and logs use UTC
body: Servers, databases and log timestamps are UTC. Convert to local time only in UI layers. Scheduled jobs are written in UTC cron expressions.

title: Cloud cost tags
summary: Every resource must carry team and env tags
body: Untagged resources are flagged weekly and removed after two warnings. Required tags: team, env, service. Budget alerts go to the owning team channel at 80 percent.

title: Office network
summary: Guest and staff SSIDs, wired desks at the hub
body: The office has separate staff and guest wireless networks. Staff devices need the device certificate installed by MDM; guests get a daily code from reception.

title: Device management
summary: MDM enforces disk encryption and OS updates
body: MDM requires full-disk encryption, screen lock after 5 minutes and OS updates within 14 days of release. Non-compliant laptops lose VPN access.

title: Logging conventions
summary: JSON logs with request ids
body: Services emit one JSON object per line with level, ts, service and request_id. Never log request bodies containing payment data.

title: Local dev ports
summary: Reserved port ranges for local services
body: Local services use ports 4000-4099 for APIs and 5170-5199 for front-ends. Harbor listens on 4010 and Pavilion on 5173.

title: Preview environments
summary: Ephemeral namespaces per pull request
body: Each pull request gets a namespace pr-<number> in kube-dev with a seeded database, destroyed 24 hours after the PR closes.

title: Decision: gRPC between backend services
summary: Internal service calls use gRPC; REST only at the edge
body: Chosen in the March architecture review. Internal calls use gRPC with protobuf contracts checked in the schemas repo. REST and GraphQL are only for external or browser clients. Rationale: typed contracts and streaming.

title: Decision: stay polyrepo
summary: Keep one repo per service, share tooling via Trellis
body: We evaluated a monorepo and declined it: CI cost and ownership boundaries mattered more than atomic refactors. Shared tooling is distributed through Trellis templates and Ferrule.

title: Decision: Postgres over MongoDB
summary: Relational store is the default for new services
body: New services default to Postgres. Document stores need a written exception because backups, tooling and on-call familiarity all assume Postgres.

title: Decision: trunk-based development
summary: Short-lived branches, merge to main daily
body: Branches live at most two days. Unfinished work merges behind a Beacon flag. Long-running release branches are not allowed.

title: Decision: semantic versioning for libraries
summary: Breaking changes only in major versions
body: Shared libraries follow semver strictly. Deprecations must survive one full minor release with a warning before removal.

title: Decision: quarterly planning cadence
summary: Plan quarterly, adjust monthly
body: Goals are set quarterly in Compass and reviewed monthly. Mid-quarter changes need the engineering manager's agreement.

title: Decision: no PII in logs
summary: Personal data must never be written to logs
body: Email addresses, names, card data and addresses are forbidden in logs. Use opaque user ids. Violations are treated as security incidents.

title: Decision: follow-the-sun on-call
summary: Two rotations cover EU and US hours
body: Rather than 24-hour single-site rotations, an EU rotation covers 06:00-14:00 UTC and a US rotation 14:00-22:00 UTC; overnight pages go to a best-effort tertiary.

title: Decision: single email vendor
summary: All transactional email through one provider
body: Consolidated on a single email provider in January to simplify deliverability monitoring. Marketing email stays on a separate tool.

title: Decision: build Beacon in-house
summary: Hosted flag vendors rejected on cost and latency
body: Hosted flag services quoted per-seat pricing and added a network hop. Beacon was built in-house with local SDK caching instead.

title: Decision: Rust only for infrastructure tools
summary: Rust allowed for single-binary tools, not product services
body: Rust is approved for Sundial-style infrastructure tools. Product services stay on Go or Python because hiring and review capacity are limited.

title: Decision: ARM for build runners
summary: Move CI to ARM for cost
body: ARM runners cut build costs by roughly 30 percent. x86-only dependencies are built on hosted runners as an exception.

title: Decision: URL-versioned external APIs
summary: Public APIs carry /v1 style prefixes
body: External APIs are versioned in the path (/v1, /v2). Old versions are supported for 12 months after a successor ships.

title: Decision: testing pyramid targets
summary: Mostly unit tests, thin end-to-end layer
body: Target mix is about 70 percent unit, 25 percent integration and 5 percent end-to-end. End-to-end tests must be deterministic or they are deleted.

title: Decision: data retention periods
summary: Customer data deleted 90 days after account closure
body: Account data is hard-deleted 90 days after closure. Invoices are kept seven years for tax reasons. Analytics events are anonymised after 13 months.

title: Decision: review requirements
summary: One approval, two for infrastructure and auth
body: Pull requests need one approving review. Changes to Cairn, Lantern or Warden need two, one from the owning team.

title: Decision: record decisions as ADRs
summary: Architecture decision records live in the docs repo
body: Significant choices are recorded as ADRs in the adr folder using the short template: context, decision, consequences. Status moves from proposed to accepted or superseded.

title: Decision: default cache TTLs
summary: Short TTLs, explicit invalidation for critical data
body: API caches default to 60 seconds. Pricing and inventory must use explicit invalidation events instead of long TTLs.

title: Decision: standard timeout budget
summary: Client timeout 2s, retries limited to 2 with jitter
body: Outbound calls default to a 2 second timeout and at most two retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Retrying non-idempotent calls is forbidden without an idempotency key.

title: Decision: money stored as integer minor units
summary: Never use floating point for currency
body: All monetary amounts are integers in minor units (cents) plus an ISO currency code. Floats are rejected in review.

title: Decision: service naming
summary: Services get a single evocative lowercase name
body: Services use one lowercase noun, registered in Gazetteer. Names are not reused after retirement.

title: Decision: accessibility baseline
summary: WCAG 2.2 AA for customer-facing UI
body: Customer-facing interfaces must meet WCAG 2.2 AA. Mosaic components ship with automated axe checks and manual keyboard review.

title: Decision: dependency update policy
summary: Weekly automated update PRs, security patches within 72 hours
body: Dependabot opens weekly update pull requests. Critical security patches must be merged within 72 hours; others within the sprint.

title: Decision: docs live with the code
summary: Reference docs in the repo, guides in Quill
body: Reference documentation sits next to the code in each repo. Narrative guides and tutorials are published through Quill.

title: Decision: internal service SLOs
summary: 99.9 percent availability for tier-1 services
body: Tier-1 services (Harbor, Pavilion, Lantern) target 99.9 percent monthly availability; tier-2 targets 99.5. Error budgets are reviewed monthly.

title: Decision: dark launches for risky changes
summary: Ship behind flags and mirror traffic first
body: Risky changes are deployed dark, traffic is mirrored for a day, and only then enabled gradually 1, 10, 50, 100 percent.

title: Decision: pairing for onboarding
summary: New hires pair for their first two weeks
body: Each new engineer pairs with a buddy for the first two weeks and ships a small change to production by day five.

title: Decision: open source license policy
summary: Permissive licenses only for dependencies
body: Allowed: MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0. Copyleft dependencies such as GPL need legal approval. License scan runs in the Trellis security step.

title: Decision: batch jobs avoid business hours
summary: Heavy jobs run between 01:00 and 05:00 UTC
body: Heavy batch work is scheduled in the 01:00-05:00 UTC window so replicas stay responsive during business hours.

title: Procedure: deploying to production
summary: Merge, wait for green, run deploy command, watch dashboards
body: 1) Merge to main. 2) Wait for the Trellis pipeline to go green. 3) Run `ferrule deploy prod <service>` from #deploys. 4) Watch the service dashboard for 15 minutes. 5) Roll back with `ferrule rollback` if error rate doubles.

title: Procedure: emergency rollback
summary: Revert to previous digest with ferrule rollback
body: Run `ferrule rollback <service> --to previous`. The deploy job pins the prior image digest; database migrations are not reversed automatically, so check the migration notes first.

title: Procedure: declaring an incident
summary: Use /incident in Slack, assign a commander and scribe
body: Type /incident in Rookery, choose severity, and a channel is created. The first responder becomes commander unless they hand off. Assign a scribe and post to Heron within 15 minutes for sev1 and sev2.

title: Procedure: blameless postmortems
summary: Write within five business days, review in the guild meeting
body: Every sev1 and sev2 gets a blameless postmortem within five business days using the template in the docs repo. Action items need owners and due dates.

title: Procedure: database schema migrations
summary: Expand, migrate, contract in separate releases
body: Schema changes use expand/contract: add the new column nullable, deploy code that writes both, backfill, switch reads, then drop the old column in a later release. Never rename a column in one step.

title: Procedure: requesting production access
summary: Request through the access portal with a ticket
body: Production access is requested in the access portal with a ticket link and manager approval. Grants expire after 30 days and are logged. Standing access is not given.

title: Procedure: releasing Brindle
summary: Cut release branch Monday, submit Tuesday
body: Brindle's release branch is cut Monday morning, QA signs off by Tuesday noon, then the builds are submitted to the stores. Hotfixes skip QA only with the engineering manager's approval.

title: Procedure: rotating API keys
summary: Issue new, deploy, revoke old within 24 hours
body: Create the new key in Warden, deploy it to consumers, confirm traffic on the new key, then revoke the old one. The overlap window must not exceed 24 hours.

title: Procedure: restoring a database from snapshot
summary: Restore into a new instance, then promote
body: Never restore over a live database. Restore the snapshot into a new instance, validate row counts, then repoint PgBouncer. Record the point-in-time target in the ticket.

title: Procedure: on-call handoff
summary: Written handoff note with open alerts and risky deploys
body: The outgoing engineer posts a handoff note: open incidents, noisy alerts, upcoming risky deploys and known flaky checks. The incoming engineer acknowledges in thread.

title: Procedure: creating a new service
summary: Run ferrule new, register in Gazetteer, add dashboards
body: Run `ferrule new service`, answer the prompts, merge the generated pull request, confirm the entry in Gazetteer and add an SLO dashboard from the template before first deploy.

title: Procedure: removing stale feature flags
summary: Delete flag code first, then the flag
body: When a flag has been 100 percent for two weeks, remove the code paths, deploy, and only then delete the flag in Beacon so old pods keep working.

title: Procedure: running a load test
summary: Announce, run Plover against staging, record results
body: Announce in #perf, scale staging to production-like size, run `k6 run checkout.js`, and attach the summary to the release ticket. Never run load tests against production.

title: Procedure: handling a vulnerability report
summary: Triage within one business day, patch by severity
body: Security reports are triaged within one business day. Severity decides the patch deadline: critical 72 hours, high 7 days, medium 30 days. Keep the reporter updated.

title: Procedure: manual certificate renewal
summary: Force renewal with cmctl when cert-manager is stuck
body: If cert-manager fails to renew, run `cmctl renew <name> -n <namespace>`, check the challenge status, and open a ticket with platform if DNS validation is failing.

title: Procedure: customer data deletion request
summary: Verify identity, run deletion job, confirm in writing
body: Verify the requester through the support tool, trigger the deletion job in Tidepool, wait for the confirmation event, then email the customer. Complete within 30 days.

title: Procedure: quarantining a flaky test
summary: Tag, ticket, fix within a sprint
body: A test that fails intermittently is tagged quarantine, a ticket is opened automatically and the owner has one sprint to fix it before it is deleted.

title: Procedure: lost or stolen laptop
summary: Report immediately, MDM remote wipe
body: Report to security within the hour. MDM issues a remote lock and wipe, VPN profile and SSH certificates are revoked, and a replacement is shipped.

title: Procedure: monthly cost review
summary: Review top ten spend lines with owners
body: On the second Thursday the platform lead reviews the ten largest cost lines with owners and records savings actions in Compass.

title: Procedure: pull request etiquette
summary: Small PRs, description with why, link the ticket
body: Keep pull requests under about 400 changed lines, explain why in the description, link the ticket and request review from the code owners file.

title: Procedure: hotfix to production
summary: Branch from the deployed tag, cherry-pick, deploy
body: Branch from the currently deployed tag, apply the minimal fix, get one approval, and deploy with `ferrule deploy prod --hotfix`. Backport to main the same day.

title: Procedure: backfilling a warehouse table
summary: Pause the DAG, run backfill with date range, verify counts
body: Pause the Tidepool DAG, run `airflow dags backfill` with an explicit date range, compare row counts against the source and unpause. Never backfill more than 30 days at once.

title: Procedure: changing a DNS record
summary: Edit in Cairn, plan, apply, verify propagation
body: Change the record in the Cairn zone module, get the plan reviewed, apply, and verify with dig against both resolvers. Lower the TTL a day ahead for cutovers.

title: Procedure: responding to a leaked secret
summary: Revoke, rotate, audit, document
body: Revoke the secret at its source first, rotate through Warden, audit access logs for use during the exposure window and write a short incident note.

title: Procedure: planning time off
summary: Announce two weeks ahead and name a deputy
body: Add time off to the team calendar, announce at least two weeks ahead for stretches over three days and name a deputy for your services.

title: History: March checkout outage
summary: Pavilion checkout failed for 47 minutes after a bad config push
body: On a Tuesday in March a Beacon flag misconfiguration disabled payment forms for 47 minutes. Root cause: no schema validation on flag payloads. Fix: validation added and dark-launch policy introduced.

title: History: Redis eviction incident
summary: State data lost when stored in the cache cluster
body: A team stored rate-limit counters in cache-redis; an eviction wave reset them and let a burst through. Led to the rule that durable state goes to state-redis only.

title: History: Postgres 14 to 16 upgrade
summary: Completed in two weekends with logical replication
body: The upgrade used logical replication to new clusters, cutover over two weekends with 90 seconds of read-only mode each. Lessons: test extension compatibility early.

title: History: Harbor rewritten from Python to Go
summary: Rewrite finished last year, latency down by 60 percent
body: Harbor started as a Django app. The Go rewrite shipped in phases over six months, cut p95 latency by about 60 percent and halved the fleet size.

title: History: switched SMS providers
summary: Moved SMS after repeated delivery failures
body: After three delivery incidents in one quarter, SMS moved to a new provider with regional routing. Delivery rate rose from 94 to 99 percent.

title: History: autumn hack day outcomes
summary: Hack day produced Rookery and the Sundial prototype
body: The autumn hack day delivered the first Rookery bot and a Sundial prototype. Both were adopted within two months.

title: History: expired internal certificate
summary: An internal CA certificate lapsed and broke service-to-service calls
body: The intermediate CA expired on a Sunday, breaking mTLS between services for 25 minutes. Now cert expiry is monitored at 30, 14 and 3 days.

title: History: failed DNS cutover
summary: A long TTL delayed the cutover by hours
body: During a load balancer migration the TTL was still 24 hours, so clients hit the old address long after cutover. Origin of the rule to lower TTL a day ahead.

title: History: CI flakiness drive
summary: Flaky failures reduced from 12 percent to 2 percent
body: A two-month effort quarantined unstable tests, pinned runner images and fixed port collisions. Pipeline failure rate from flakes dropped from 12 to 2 percent.

title: History: pricing rounding bug
summary: Float rounding overcharged some orders by one cent
body: A float-based discount calculation overcharged roughly 0.3 percent of orders by one cent. Refunded automatically; led to the integer minor units rule.

title: History: hiring freeze last winter
summary: Hiring paused for a quarter, projects reprioritised
body: Hiring was frozen for one quarter. Brindle features were postponed and Juniper work was reduced to maintenance.

title: History: secrets audit findings
summary: Audit found 14 stale static credentials
body: The security audit found 14 long-lived static credentials; all were rotated and moved behind Warden within a month.

title: History: Kubernetes 1.28 to 1.30
summary: Upgrade done cluster by cluster, no customer impact
body: Dev first, then stage, then prod over three weeks. A deprecated API in an old Helm chart caused one failed deploy, fixed by upgrading the chart.

title: History: Black Friday capacity
summary: Pre-scaled 3x and held 1,900 orders per minute
body: For the sales peak we pre-scaled Harbor and Orrery threefold, froze deploys for four days and sustained 1,900 orders per minute with p95 under 400 ms.

title: History: failed reindex
summary: Reindex filled disk and crashed the search cluster
body: A full reindex doubled index size, filled the data nodes and crashed Sieve for an hour. Now reindexing uses aliases and requires 2x free disk.

title: History: team reorganisation
summary: Payments and Platform split into separate teams
body: Payments (Harbor, Ledgerlint, Marlin) and Platform (Cairn, Kiln, Trellis) became separate teams after the reorganisation.

title: History: tabletop breach exercise
summary: Exercise exposed a missing escalation contact
body: The tabletop breach drill found no documented escalation contact for legal after hours. A rotation list was added to the incident template.

title: History: App Store rejection
summary: Brindle rejected for missing account deletion flow
body: An App Store review rejected Brindle because in-app account deletion was missing. Added within a week, then approved.

title: History: stale CDN assets
summary: Missing purge left an old logo online for a day
body: A rebrand shipped but the purge step was skipped, so the old logo stayed on the edge for 24 hours. Purge-by-tag is now part of the deploy job.

title: History: notification queue backlog
summary: A stuck consumer delayed emails by six hours
body: A poison message blocked a Notifier consumer, delaying emails six hours. Added dead-letter handling with max-deliver of 5.

title: History: cloud cost spike
summary: Orphaned load test cluster cost 18k in a month
body: A load-test cluster was left running after a test and cost about 18k in a month. Led to automatic expiry tags on non-prod resources.

title: History: on-call load review
summary: Pages per week halved after alert tuning
body: A review found the primary averaged 31 pages a week. After deleting noisy alerts and adding runbook links it fell to 14.

title: History: GDPR readiness review
summary: Completed review produced the retention policy

title: Code hosting (2024)

title: Code hosting (2026)
summary: Source code now lives on GitHub; GitLab is read-only
body: Since the September migration all repositories live on GitHub under the acme organisation. The old GitLab server is read-only and will be shut down; use pull requests.

title: Team chat tool (2023)
summary: Engineering chat runs on Mattermost
body: Day-to-day engineering chat happens in a self-hosted Mattermost server; incident channels are created there.

title: Team chat tool (current)
summary: Engineering chat moved from Mattermost to Slack
body: All engineering chat is on Slack since the spring consolidation. Mattermost was archived, and Rookery runs there.

title: Primary region (early setup)
summary: Everything runs in a single region, eu-west-1
body: All production workloads run in eu-west-1 only. Disaster recovery means restoring from backups into the same region.

title: Primary regions (current)
summary: Production is active in two regions: eu-west-1 and us-east-1
body: Production is active-active across eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Failover is automatic for stateless services; databases fail over with a manual promotion.

title: Deploy tooling (legacy)
summary: Deployments are done with Spinnaker pipelines
body: Services are deployed through Spinnaker pipelines triggered from the CI job. Rollbacks use the Spinnaker UI.

title: Deploy tooling (current)
summary: Deploys use the ferrule command; Spinnaker is retired
body: Deployment is `ferrule deploy` from the chat channel or the CI job. The Spinnaker installation was decommissioned in July.

title: Python standard (2024)
summary: Services standardise on Python 3.9
body: The supported Python version for services is 3.9, using pip and requirements files with pip-tools.

title: Python standard (current)
summary: Python 3.12 is the standard, 3.9 is end of life
body: Python 3.12 with uv is the standard for services. Version 3.9 is end of life; remaining services must upgrade this quarter.

title: Page acknowledgement window (old)
summary: Primary on-call has 15 minutes to acknowledge
body: If the primary does not acknowledge a page within 15 minutes it escalates to the secondary.

title: Page acknowledgement window (current)
summary: Primary on-call now has 5 minutes to acknowledge
body: The acknowledgement window was cut to 5 minutes after the March incident review; the secondary is paged after that.

title: Staging database host (2025)
summary: Staging database is stage-db-01
body: Staging uses one Postgres server, stage-db-01, reached through the VPN on the default port.

title: Staging database host (current)
summary: Staging database is the stage-pg cluster behind PgBouncer
body: Staging now uses the stage-pg cluster behind PgBouncer; stage-db-01 was retired. Connect through the pooler, never the nodes.

title: Log retention (old)
summary: Logs are kept for 7 days
body: Loki keeps logs for 7 days. Anything older must be exported manually before it disappears.

title: Log retention (current)
summary: Logs are kept for 30 days
body: Loki retention was raised to 30 days after the audit; archive older data to the cold bucket on request.

title: Team standup time (old)
summary: Daily standup is at 09:30
body: The platform team's daily standup is 09:30 UTC in the video room.

title: Team standup time (current)
summary: Daily standup moved to 10:15
body: Daily standup moved to 10:15 UTC so the US team can join. It is skipped on release Tuesdays.

title: Brindle release cadence (2024)
summary: Brindle ships monthly
body: Brindle releases once a month on the first Monday, with a QA week before.

title: Brindle release cadence (current)
summary: Brindle ships every second Tuesday
body: Release cadence is every second Tuesday since the QA automation landed; the monthly cycle is gone.

title: Feature flag tool (2023)
summary: Flags are managed in the LaunchLite hosted service
body: Feature flags are toggled in the hosted LaunchLite dashboard and read by its SDK.

title: Feature flag tool (current)
summary: Flags are managed in Beacon; LaunchLite was cancelled
body: All flags were migrated to Beacon and the LaunchLite subscription ended. Use the Beacon SDKs.

title: Error budget review (old)
summary: Error budgets are reviewed quarterly
body: Teams review error budget burn once a quarter in the reliability guild.

title: Error budget review (current)
summary: Error budgets are reviewed monthly
body: Review moved to monthly in the March reliability review; quarterly was too slow to change behaviour.

title: Password manager (2023)
summary: Team passwords stored in the Vaultline app
body: Shared team credentials are kept in the Vaultline password manager with per-team folders.

title: Password manager (current)
summary: Team passwords moved to Keyring Pro
body: Vaultline was replaced by Keyring Pro with SSO login. Export your folders before the old tenant closes.

title: Sprint length (old)
summary: Sprints last three weeks
body: The team runs three week sprints with planning on the first Monday.

title: Sprint length (current)
summary: Sprints last two weeks
body: Sprints were shortened to two weeks last quarter to improve feedback cycles; planning is still on Mondays.

title: Error tracking (2023)
summary: Exceptions are reported to self-hosted Raven
body: Application exceptions go to a self-hosted Raven server with a 30 day retention.

title: Error tracking (current)
summary: Exceptions are reported to the hosted Kestrel service
body: Raven was shut down; all exceptions now go to hosted Kestrel using the shared DSN from Warden.

title: Database connection details: staging
summary: How to connect to the staging Postgres through PgBouncer
body: Connect to stage-pg.example.internal on port 6432 through PgBouncer in transaction mode using a Warden lease. Staging data is synthetic.

title: Database connection details: production
summary: How to connect to the production Postgres through PgBouncer
body: Connect to prod-pg.example.internal on port 6433 through PgBouncer in transaction mode using a Warden lease. Access is read-only unless an incident is open.

title: Deploy checklist: Harbor
summary: Pre-deploy checks for the billing service
body: Before deploying Harbor confirm Ledgerlint is not mid-run, webhooks queue is empty and the payment sandbox contract tests pass.

title: Deploy checklist: Pavilion
summary: Pre-deploy checks for the storefront
body: Before deploying Pavilion confirm no marketing campaign launches within the hour, the catalog schema contract passes and the CDN purge token is valid.

title: Signing keys: iOS
summary: Where the iOS signing identities are stored
body: iOS distribution certificate and provisioning profiles are stored in the match repository, encrypted, and fetched by the release job.

title: Signing keys: Android
summary: Where the Android upload keystore is stored
body: The Android upload keystore sits in Warden under the mobile path; the Play-managed app signing key never leaves the store.

title: On-call contacts: EU rotation
summary: Escalation contacts for the EU on-call rotation
body: EU rotation escalates to the Lisbon engineering manager, then the platform lead. Handoff is at 14:00 UTC.

title: On-call contacts: US rotation
summary: Escalation contacts for the US on-call rotation
body: US rotation escalates to the Austin engineering manager, then the head of infrastructure. Handoff is at 22:00 UTC.

title: Grafana dashboard: Harbor
summary: Where to find the Harbor service dashboard
body: The Harbor dashboard folder shows invoice throughput, webhook lag and payment error rate. Linked from the Gazetteer entry.

title: Grafana dashboard: Orrery
summary: Where to find the Orrery service dashboard
body: The Orrery dashboard folder shows feature lookup latency, Redis hit ratio and snapshot freshness. Linked from the Gazetteer entry.

title: Lint rules: Python
summary: Ruff rule selection for Python repositories
body: Python repos enable ruff rules E, F, I, B and S, line length 100, and run ruff format in CI.

title: Lint rules: Go
summary: golangci-lint linters for Go repositories
body: Go repos enable govet, staticcheck, errcheck and gosec through the shared golangci config and fail CI on any finding.

title: Alert: Harbor latency
summary: Threshold for the Harbor p95 latency alert
body: Pages when Harbor p95 latency exceeds 800 ms for 10 minutes. First check the replica lag and PgBouncer saturation.

title: Alert: Harbor error rate
summary: Threshold for the Harbor error rate alert
body: Pages when Harbor 5xx rate exceeds 2 percent for 5 minutes. First check the card processor status and recent deploys.

title: Backups: Postgres
summary: Postgres snapshot schedule and verification
body: Postgres snapshots run nightly; a weekly job restores the latest into a scratch instance and runs checksum queries.

title: Backups: OpenSearch
summary: OpenSearch snapshot schedule and verification
body: OpenSearch snapshots go to the snapshot bucket every six hours; verification is a monthly restore of one index, since indexes can be rebuilt.

title: Access approval: staging
summary: Who approves staging access
body: Staging access is approved by the team lead, granted for 90 days and renewable without a ticket.

title: Access approval: production
summary: Who approves production access
body: Production access needs the team lead and the security on-call, is granted for 30 days and every renewal needs a new ticket.

title: Failover: cache Redis
summary: Failing over the cache Redis cluster
body: For cache-redis, promote the replica and accept the cold cache; no data recovery is attempted. Applications must tolerate misses.

title: Failover: state Redis
summary: Failing over the state Redis cluster
body: For state-redis, wait for replica sync, promote with the sentinel command, then verify persistence files. Data loss must be reported as an incident.

title: Changing an email template
summary: Process for editing transactional email templates
body: Edit the MJML source in Saffron, send a rendering test to the inbox testing tool, get a design review and release through Trellis.

title: Changing an SMS template
summary: Process for editing SMS templates
body: SMS templates are plain text in notifier-templates; keep under 160 characters, check the regional sender registration and release through Trellis.

title: Preview builds: Quill
summary: How preview builds work for the docs site
body: Every Quill pull request gets a static preview at a pr-<number> subdomain on the docs preview host, deleted at merge.

title: Preview builds: Pavilion
summary: How preview builds work for the storefront
body: Pavilion pull requests deploy to a namespace with seeded catalog data and a stubbed checkout, destroyed 24 hours after close.
